note: Shortens to buen before a masculine noun: un buen día.

sent.en: It is a good restaurant.

note: Shortens to mal before a masculine noun.

sent.en: I had a bad day today.

note: Shortens to gran before any singular noun, where it means great rather than big.

sent.en: I need a bigger suitcase.

note: Chiquito is the everyday Colombian word.

sent.en: I live in a small flat.

note: Before the noun it leans towards another rather than brand new.

sent.en: I bought a new car.

note: Blunt about people; mayor is the polite word for an older person.

sent.en: That building is very old.

note: Plural jóvenes, which gains an accent.

sent.en: He is too young to drive.

note: A false friend: it means long, not large.

sent.es: El camino es más {largo} de lo que pensaba.
sent.en: The road is longer than I thought.

note: For length. bajo is short in height.

sent.en: It was a short meeting.

note: Also does volume: habla más alto.

sent.en: My brother is very tall.

note: Also a preposition meaning under.

sent.en: The ceiling is very low.
That hotel is too expensive.

note: Económico is the politer word.

sent.en: I found a cheap flight.

note: Plural fáciles.

sent.es: El examen fue más {fácil} de lo esperado.
sent.en: The exam was easier than expected.

note: Plural difíciles.

sent.en: It is hard to understand at first.

note: Doubles as the adverb: camina rápido.

sent.en: I need a quick answer.

note: Despacio is the adverb you will hear more.

sent.en: The internet is very slow today.

note: For things. For weather use hace calor, and for a person estar caliente means something else entirely.

sent.en: The water is hot.

note: Also a noun: hace frío, it is cold; tengo frío, I am cold.

sent.en: The beer is nice and cold.

note: limpiar is the verb.

sent.en: The room is clean now.
These plates are dirty.

note: Lindo is more common in Colombia.

sent.en: What a lovely view.

note: Also used for weather and situations.

sent.en: The weather is nasty today.

note: Same for both genders.

sent.en: It is important to arrive on time.

note: lo antes posible is as soon as possible.

sent.en: Is it possible to change the date?

note: Also a noun: insurance.

sent.en: I am not sure of the address.

note: Colours go after the noun and agree: la casa amarilla.

sent.en: The yellow taxi is waiting.
I prefer red wine.

note: Same for both genders. Also means unripe.

sent.en: The light is green.

note: Same for both genders. Plural azules.

sent.en: He has blue eyes.
I like black coffee.

note: Also a blank space.

sent.en: I need a blank sheet of paper.

note: With estar, not ser: how you are now.

sent.en: I am very pleased with the result.

note: Bravo also means angry in Colombia, not brave.

sent.en: He is angry with me.

note: preocuparse is to worry.

sent.en: I am worried about the exam.
I get nervous before speaking.

note: estar aburrido is bored; ser aburrido is boring. Worth getting right.

sent.en: The film was boring.

note: With estar.

sent.es: No fui a trabajar porque estaba {enfermo}.
sent.en: I did not go to work because I was ill.

note: m. tengo dolor de cabeza is I have a headache.

sent.en: I have a pain in my back.

note: f.

sent.en: My head hurts.

note: f. despite ending in o: la mano.

sent.en: Give me your hand.

note: m. ¡Ojo! on its own means watch out.

sent.en: Something got in my eye.

note: m. a pie means on foot.

sent.en: Let us walk, it is nearby.

note: Works like gustar: me duele, it hurts me.

sent.en: My legs hurt.

note: m. Doctor is also used, and is how you address them.

sent.en: I have an appointment with the doctor tomorrow.

note: Shortens to un before a masculine noun: un café.

sent.en: There is only one left.
I want two black coffees, please.
We arrive in three hours.
There are four of us.
See you at five.
It costs ten thousand pesos.
I have twenty minutes free.

note: cien exactly; ciento in 101 to 199.

sent.en: There are more than a hundred people.

note: Never un mil, just mil. You will use it constantly with pesos.

sent.en: Lunch costs fifteen thousand.

note: Shortens to primer before a masculine noun.

sent.en: It is the first time I have come.

note: The final one. pasado is last as in previous.

sent.en: This is the last bus.

note: media hora is half an hour. mitad is the noun.

sent.en: Wait half an hour for me.

note: ahorita in Colombia can mean in a minute or just now, and is gloriously vague.

sent.en: I cannot talk now.
I am not working today.

note: Both. la mañana is the morning, mañana on its own is tomorrow.

sent.en: I will see you early tomorrow.
I was at the office yesterday.

note: f. buenas noches is both good evening and good night.

sent.es: Anoche no dormí en toda la {noche}.
sent.en: Last night I did not sleep all night.

note: m. despite the a: el día. todos los días is every day.

sent.en: It was a very long day.

note: f. fin de semana is weekend.

sent.en: Last week I was ill.

note: m. Plural meses.

sent.en: Next month I am travelling to Peru.

note: m. The ñ matters: ano without it is something else.

sent.en: I have been here a year.

note: f. ¿Qué hora es? is what time is it.

sent.es: La {hora} de salida es a las tres.
sent.en: The departure time is at three.

note: m.

sent.en: Give me a minute.
I get up very early.

note: Also a noun: la tarde, the afternoon. buenas tardes.

sent.en: I arrived late to the meeting.

sent.es: El {próximo} tren sale en veinte minutos.
sent.en: The next train leaves in twenty minutes.

note: el año pasado is last year.

sent.en: Last month it rained a lot.

note: f. llover is the verb: está lloviendo.

sent.es: La {lluvia} no paró en toda la tarde.
sent.en: The rain did not stop all afternoon.

note: m. hace sol is it is sunny.

sent.en: It is very sunny today.

note: m. despite the a. Tiempo also means weather.

sent.en: The weather here changes every hour.

note: m.

sent.en: We swam in the river on Sunday.

note: f.

sent.es: La {montaña} se ve desde la ventana.
sent.en: The mountain is visible from the window.

note: f.

sent.en: We spent the day at the beach.

note: m. Plural árboles.

sent.es: Hay un {árbol} enorme en el patio.
sent.en: There is an enormous tree in the garden.

note: m. perra for a female, though it is also an insult.

sent.es: El {perro} del vecino ladra toda la noche.
sent.en: The neighbour's dog barks all night.

note: m. Also a car jack.

sent.en: My cat sleeps all day.
A black coffee, please.

note: Always plural. muchas gracias is thank you very much.

sent.en: Thank you very much for the help.

note: For bumping into someone or interrupting. Lo siento is for real regret.

sent.en: Excuse me, can I get past?

note: The h is silent.

sent.en: Hello, how are you?

note: Chao is far more common in Colombia.

sent.en: Goodbye, see you soon.

note: Plural in Spanish. Buenas on its own works any time of day.

sent.en: Good morning, how can I help you?

note: Said when leaving a room or squeezing past. Very Colombian.

sent.en: Excuse me, I am off now.

note: Informal. ¿Qué más? is the Colombian version.

sent.en: How is it going? How is everything?

sent.es: El viaje es largo pero {vale la pena}.
sent.en: The journey is long but it is worth it.
